A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TokenSelect and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original attention analyses, benchmark evaluations, ablations, and latency measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds TokenSelect evaluations, including Qwen2-72B results. Some comparator scores are explicitly attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: Per-head soft voting, chunk-wise prefill selection, Selection Cache decoding, and the Paged Dot Product Kernel are retained. New Algorithm 2 documents the existing kernel; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate InfiniteBench, RULER, English LongBench tasks, and extended R.PK/R.KV contexts up to 2M tokens. Added model configurations reuse existing tasks. The 2M experiment moves from Section 6.6 to Appendix B.1.

E2.justification: Table 3 expands from the post-trained model and MInference comparison to include SnapKV, InfiniGen, QUEST, RetrievalAttention, StreamingLLM, InfLLM, and static-pattern MInference. Appendix E adds an H2O comparison. Several added baseline outcomes are sourced from prior work, rather than established as reruns. The earlier post-trained LongBench comparison disappears.

E3.justification: Added settings include TokenSelect on Llama-3-8B-Instruct-262k, an SDPA 128K control, and Qwen2-72B with tensor parallelism of four. The threshold analysis adds a theta=1.0 setting. Existing benchmark metrics, greedy decoding, and default token budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 9 extends the existing cache-threshold analysis to all nine InfiniteBench tasks and includes theta=1.0. Appendix B.2 adds a model-size scalability check on Qwen2-72B. Existing selection-function ablations, token-budget sensitivity, and 2M-context analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, or reports confidence intervals or significance tests for benchmark comparisons. Greedy decoding and the descriptive distributions in Figure 3 are unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial comparison, 72B, and threshold results while dropping the post-trained LongBench scores from Table 3. New Table 6 reports 72B R.KV scores of 88.12 versus NTK's 50.00, with latencies of 63.27 versus 111.98 seconds. Retained benchmark tables and figures are unchanged. New Table 9 reports R.KV=86.20 at theta=0.95, conflicting with approximately 87.6 in retained Figure 6d.

T1.justification: The selective sparse attention definition and Lemma 1's assumptions, statement, and proof are unchanged mathematically. The proof moves from Appendix A to C, and the inference equations move to Appendix D.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free inference and length-extrapolation contributions, serving-system compatibility claim, and headline speedups of 23.84x and 2.28x. Added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges that short benchmark generations prevent precise measurement of Selection Cache's end-to-end speedup. It adds larger-model applicability discussion and elaborates H2O's limitations. It removes v2's interpretation that MInference cannot reverse post-training's negative effect on LongBench; Section 8's limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 2 newly specifies kernel tensor shapes, head indexing, block processing, and HBM/SRAM transfers. Algorithm 1 gains explicit input domains, and Table 6 specifies tensor parallelism of four. These expand documentation; the existing software stack, hardware disclosures, and code URL are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds RetrievalAttention, ShadowKV, and newer application references, while removing the KV quantization/merging discussion and citations such as KIVI, MiniCache, and CaM. Appendix E expands positioning against H2O. The central distinction between dynamic token selection and earlier sparse-attention approaches remains.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes existing material: the inference overview, Selection Cache algorithm, and 2M experiment move into appendices, and hyperparameter analysis merges into the ablation section. Introduction, related-work, and implementation passages are edited. Author information changes, and acknowledgments and an AI-use statement are added.

P2.justification: Table 3 becomes a substantially larger comparison grouped by model. v3 adds Tables 6, 7, and 9 and Algorithm 2, relocates Algorithm 1 and Figure 9, and adjusts display sizes and placement. All nine existing figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The comparison using the same post-trained backbone, 72B evaluation, and kernel pseudocode strengthen applicability evidence and implementation transparency. The explicit Selection Cache speedup limitation also improves qualification. These gains outweigh the narrower post-trained LongBench comparison, but reliance on cited baseline scores and the unresolved Table 9/Figure 6 discrepancy limit the improvement.
